verdict: Hims & Hers grew revenue just 4% to $608M as U.S. sales fell 8% during its weight-loss pivot, and restructuring, legal and deal costs swung it to a $92M loss — even as international revenue jumped nearly tenfold to $78M.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $608M, vs $586M a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs +$0.20 a year ago — the company made a loss this quarter

kpis.label: Subscribers
kpis.note: Up 9% YoY — people on a recurring subscription plan at quarter end

kpis.label: International revenue
kpis.note: Up 969% YoY, from $7M — the ZAVA and LIVWELL acquisitions

segments.name: United States
segments.note: Sales in the US — mostly online telehealth (care by app or phone) for weight loss, hair, skin and other treatments, plus the products that go with them. Down 8% as the weight-loss offering shifted toward branded GLP-1 medicines, with compounded versions offered only on a limited scale.

segments.name: Rest of the world
segments.note: Sales outside the US. Up nearly tenfold, mainly because of acquisitions — ZAVA in Europe and LIVWELL — as the company builds an international business.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Ads and the cost of signing up new customers — the biggest running cost, though a smaller share of sales than a year ago (37% vs 39%).

opex.name: Operations and support
opex.note: Fulfilling orders, running pharmacies and supporting customers. Up 53% YoY as volumes and acquired businesses grew.

opex.name: Technology and development
opex.note: Building the app, website and AI clinical tools, and paying the engineers behind them.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and admin. More than doubled YoY; it includes $15M of legal settlement costs and $13M of acquisition costs (see one-offs).

takeaways.title: The U.S. engine stalled
takeaways.text: U.S. revenue fell 8% as the weight-loss business pivoted from compounded GLP-1s to branded medicines. Monthly revenue per subscriber slipped to $80 from $85.

takeaways.title: Margins compressed
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell to 65% from 73% a year ago — product costs rose in the pivot, and cost of revenue absorbed $28M of inventory write-downs tied to it.

takeaways.title: Cash still flowed
takeaways.text: Despite the $92M GAAP loss, Adjusted EBITDA was +$44M and free cash flow +$53M — much of the loss is one-off charges and non-cash items, listed below.

oneTimers: Restructuring and other charges of $33M tied to the 2026 shift in the U.S. weight-loss offering toward branded GLP-1 medicines — including $28M of inventory write-downs inside cost of revenue.

General and administrative costs include $15M of legal settlement costs and $13M of acquisition and transaction-related costs (per the company's Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation) — items it treats as non-recurring.
otherDetail: Other expense was $23.2M, net: the value of liabilities Hims & Hers owes rose by $17.6M and its equity securities fell in value by $9.7M, partly offset by $4.1M of other income, net.
footerNote: Filed in thousands; shown in $M to three decimals so the lines add up.
